Adampol – Polonezköy

Zofia Ryży Memorial House ('Aunt Zosia's House')

To the whole village she was 'Aunt Zosia' – and, Poland's ambassador said, it was thanks to her that Polish did not die out in Adampol.

Theme
Adampol – Polonezköy
District
Beykoz
Period
1881–1883 / 1940
Visiting
Limited access

The story

In 1940 a priest from Adampol wrote out a baptism certificate for Leopold Mueckenbrunn, a Polish Jew from Bielsko – and named Zofia Ryży as godmother. In 2021 Poland's ambassador to Turkey, Jakub Kumoch, described such documents signed by Fr Antoni Wojdas: they were probably fictitious, meant to help Jews fleeing Europe obtain visas. Zofia is the only real person among the godparents listed. Her family and neighbours knew nothing of it. Fr Wojdas most likely worked with Consul General Wojciech Rychlewicz, who issued refugees with certificates of Catholic faith.

How to visit

The house is on the village's main street, about 200 m east of the church, on the south side of the road. The façade and restored fence are easy to see from the street. The interior opens only on certain days and at hours that change – ask the Polish consulate in Istanbul or the parish before you go. It is a house museum in a lived-in village: please do not enter the grounds when it is closed.
